title: Runtime LTS patch release notes template
author: Elliot Price
body:
## Purpose
This page is the standard template for **Runtime LTS patch release notes** (e.g., `runtime-1.20-lts.3`).

LTS notes are written for enterprise operations teams and platform engineers. They prioritize:
- What changed and why it matters
- Upgrade risk and mitigations
- Compatibility and known issues
- Clear upgrade/rollback instructions

> Guidance: Assume the reader is pinning versions and has a change-management process. Avoid “internal refactor” noise. Every bullet should map to a customer-observable outcome or a reliability/security guarantee.

---

# Runtime LTS Patch Release Notes: <RUNTIME_LTS_VERSION>
**Example:** `runtime-1.20-lts.3`

**Release date:** <YYYY-MM-DD>

**Branch / tag:** <git ref>
- LTS branch: `<runtime-X.Y-lts>`
- Patch tag: `<runtime-X.Y-lts.Z>`

**Owner (Release Engineering):** <name>
**Runtime approver:** <name>
**SRE go/no-go:** <name>

**Artifacts:**
- Container image(s): `<registry>/<image>:<tag>`
- Private artifacts bundle (if applicable): `<location>`
- SBOM / provenance attestation: `<link>`

**Support window:** Per ADR-0097, this LTS line is supported until <YYYY-MM-DD>.

---

## Executive summary (1–2 paragraphs)
<Describe the intent of this patch release in plain language.>

**What you should do:**
- Recommended for: <who should upgrade>

## Customer impact
### Who is impacted
- Deployment modes: Hosted / Dedicated / Private (circle all that apply)
- Hardware: <A100/H100/L4/etc.>
- Workloads: <chat / embeddings / long context / tool calling / batching>
- Regions (if applicable): <regions>

### Observable changes
- <Example: Reduced tail latency for long prompts under continuous batching>
- <Example: Fixes intermittent scheduler deadlock causing 5xx spikes>

### Downtime / restart requirements
- Requires runtime restart: <yes/no>
- Control plane changes required: <yes/no>
- Rolling restart supported: <yes/no; constraints>

---

## Risk level
**Release risk:** <Low | Medium | High>

### Risk rubric (include in all releases)
- **Low:** Narrow bug/security fix; no behavior changes; perf deltas within noise; standard canary clean.
- **Medium:** Touches scheduling/batching/KV cache behavior; known edge cases; mitigations available; canary required.
- **High:** Changes to request routing/queueing, memory management, kernel selection, or serialization; requires extended canary and explicit customer comms.

### Why this release is rated <X>
- <Reason 1>
- <Reason 2>

### Rollback confidence
- Rollback path validated: <yes/no>
- Expected rollback time: <estimate>
- Rollback caveats: <any restrictions>

- API compatibility statement: <No breaking changes expected / describe deltas>

## What changed in this patch
> Rules:
> 1) Group by customer-facing category.
> 2) Include “why it matters” per item.
> 3) Link every item to the tracking source (GitHub PR, Linear issue, Jira SUP where appropriate).

### Security fixes
| Item | Severity | Affected versions | Customer action | References |

| <Short description> | <Critical/High/Medium/Low> | <range> | <upgrade/config change> | <CVE if any>, <PR link>, <internal tracking> |

### Correctness / reliability
| Item | Customer symptom | Fix summary | Risk notes | References |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <Deadlock under bursty load> | <e.g., elevated 5xx, stuck requests> | <short> | <any caveats> | <PR>, <Linear>, <SUP> |

### Performance (latency/throughput)
| Item | Baseline issue | Improvement | Potential trade-offs | References |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <KV cache compaction> | <p99 spikes> | <p99 -12% at N=...> | <slightly higher VRAM> | <PR>, <benchmark link> |

### Operational / observability
| Item | What changed | Why it matters | References |

### Not included (explicit exclusions)
List noteworthy items that were considered but **intentionally excluded** from this patch to keep change surface area small.
- <Example: Refactor of scheduler queue implementation (deferred to non-LTS train)>
- <Example: New kernel path for <arch> (not LTS-eligible)>

---

## Behavior changes
> Only include if user-visible. If “none”, say so explicitly.

- Behavior changes: <None | describe>
- Backwards compatibility notes: <describe>

Examples of behavior changes worth calling out:
- Different batching grouping that can affect token interleaving
- Changes to truncation, stop sequence behavior, or streaming chunk boundaries
- Changed defaults for timeouts/retries or queue limits

## Upgrade instructions
> Provide explicit, copy/paste-able steps for each supported deployment mode. If a mode is not applicable, state “N/A”.

### Hosted API (N/A for most customers)
- <If applicable: who is auto-upgraded, comms, expected timing>

### Dedicated (Redwood-managed)
- Change window required: <yes/no>
- Redwood action: <what Redwood will do>
- Customer action: <what customer must do>
- Verification steps:
  1. <health check>
  2. <smoke test prompt set>
  3. <check dashboards>

### Private (VPC / on-prem)
**Prerequisites**
- Installer version: `>= <x.y>`
- Helm chart version (if applicable): `>= <x.y>`
- Disk space / node drain requirements: <notes>

**Step-by-step**
1. Pin the runtime image tag to `<runtime-X.Y-lts.Z>`.
2. Apply manifests / run installer with the pinned version.
3. Perform rolling restart (or full restart) per the Private guide.
4. Validate:
   - `/healthz` and `/readyz`
   - <synthetic request test>
   - Error rate < threshold
   - Latency within baseline bands

**Post-upgrade validation (required)**
- Run <named smoke suite> against production-like prompts.
- Confirm dashboards/alerts are green for <duration>.

---

## Rollback instructions
### Rollback target
- Roll back to: `<runtime-X.Y-lts.(Z-1)>` (or `<explicit version>`)

### Rollback procedure (Private)
1. Re-pin runtime image tag to the rollback target.
2. Apply manifests / run installer.
3. Validate health checks and key metrics.

### Rollback caveats
- <Example: Rolling back crosses a state format boundary (rare; should be avoided in LTS).>
